The '''United States Penitentiary, Allenwood''', also known as '''USP Allenwood''', is a [[Incarceration in the United States#Security levels|maximum security]] United States federal prison in [[Pennsylvania]]. It is part of the [[Allenwood Federal Correctional Complex]] (FCC Allenwood) and is operated by the [[Federal Bureau of Prisons]], a division of the [[United States Department of Justice]].

FCC Allenwood is located on [[U.S. Route 15]] in [[Gregg Township, Union County, Pennsylvania|Gregg Township]], [[Union County, Pennsylvania|Union County]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www2.census.gov/geo/maps/DC2020/DC20BLK/st42_pa/cousub/cs4211931480_gregg/DC20BLK_CS4211931480.pdf|title=2020 CENSUS - CENSUS BLOCK MAP: Gregg township, PA|publisher=[[U.S. Census Bureau]]|access-date=2022-08-14|quote=Allenwood Federal Correctional Complx}}</ref> near White Deer. It is approximately halfway between the cities of [[Williamsport, Pennsylvania|Williamsport]] and [[Lewisburg, Pennsylvania|Lewisburg]] and approximately {{convert|75|mi|km|round=5|abbr=off|sp=us}} north of [[Harrisburg, Pennsylvania]], the state capital.<ref>{{cite web|title=USP Allenwood|url=http://www.bop.gov/locations/institutions/alp/index.jsp|publisher=Federal Bureau of Prisons}}</ref>

==Facility and programs==
USP Allenwood has four two-level housing units each of which consists of four 16-cell ranges around a central dayroom where inmates can congregate during the times they are allowed outside their cells. Most cells house two inmates each.  Recreational and counseling facilities are located adjacent to the housing units. The outer perimeter is secured by a double line of fencing with rolled barbed wire on the ground in between the fences. The inner fence is equipped with a perimeter intrusion detection system and a road for patrol vehicles runs along the outer fence. Correction officers man six guard towers at each corner of the security fence and a seventh within the fence.<ref>{{cite book|last=Bosworth|first=Mary|title=The US Federal Prison System|year=2002|publisher=SAGE|location=Thousand Oaks, CA|isbn=9780761923046|pages=[https://archive.org/details/usfederalprisons0000bosw/page/375 375]|url=https://archive.org/details/usfederalprisons0000bosw/page/375}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Spens|first=Iona|title=The Architecture of Incarceration|year=1994|publisher=Academy Editions|location=London|isbn=9781854903587|pages=128}}</ref>

Educational programs include [[GED]], [[ESL]], adult continuing education, vocational training, correspondence classes, and evening college classes. Inmates work in a UNICOR upholstery factory and institutional maintenance jobs such as food service and building repair. Medical, psychological and drug treatment services are also available.<ref>{{cite book|last=Bosworth|first=Mary|title=The US Federal Prison System|year=2002|publisher=SAGE|location=Thousand Oaks, CA|isbn=9780761923046|pages=[https://archive.org/details/usfederalprisons0000bosw/page/375 375]|url=https://archive.org/details/usfederalprisons0000bosw/page/375}}</ref>

==Incidents==

===1996 murder===
In April 1996, USP Allenwood inmate [[David Paul Hammer]] allegedly strangled fellow inmate Andrew Hunt Marti to death with a piece of homemade cord. Hammer and Marti were cellmates in the Special Housing Unit, where especially violent inmates are held. Writing on a website dedicated to his case in 2001, Hammer could not ‘attribute any motive’ to his actions. Hammer, a career criminal who was serving a 1,200-year sentence for crimes including larceny, shooting with intent to kill, kidnapping and making bomb threats, subsequently pleaded guilty to Marti's murder and was sentenced to death by the electric chair.<ref>{{cite web|title=DAVID PAUL HAMMER, PETITIONER V. JOHN D. ASHCROFT, ET AL.|url=https://www.prisonlegalnews.org/media/litigation/hammer_v._ashcroft_pln_amicus_media_brief.pdf|publisher=US Department of Justice}}</ref>

The death sentence was vacated in 2006 after a federal judge found that prosecutors withheld evidence during the penalty phase that would have bolstered Hammer's claim that he and Marti were having consensual sex.  In July 2014, another federal judge concurred, ruling that a life sentence was appropriate based upon multiple circumstances, including Hammer's acceptance of responsibility and remorsefulness, his extended family history of dysfunction, abuse and mental illness, his mental and emotional impairments and his self-improvement, specifically citing Hammer's writing to at-risk children and counseling them against engaging in criminal conduct.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Beauge|first1=John|title=Admitted murderer of Allenwood cell mate no longer facing execution|url=http://www.pennlive.com/midstate/index.ssf/2014/07/admitted_murderer_of_allenwood_1.html|website=Penn Live|publisher=PA Media Group|access-date=18 October 2015|date=July 17, 2014}}</ref>

===2005 murder===
On September 28, 2005, USP Allenwood inmates Ritz Williams (47085-008) and Shawn Cooya (48896-008) stabbed a fellow inmate, 50-year-old Alvin Allery, ten times with a homemade knife and repeatedly kicked him in the head and torso, causing Allery's death. Williams and Cooya were already serving lengthy sentences, Williams for murder and Cooya for weapons violations. A subsequent investigation revealed that Williams and Cooya planned the attack in advance. In 2013, Williams and Cooya pleaded guilty to [[first-degree murder]] and were sentenced to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole.<ref>{{cite web|last=Walker|first=R.A.|title=Two indicted for 2005 killing at Allenwood prison complex|url=http://www.sungazette.com/page/content.detail/id/505623/Two-indicted-for-2005-killing-at-Allenwood-prison-complex.html|publisher=Williamsport Sun-Gazette (PA)|access-date=12 October 2013|date=February 15, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140303075838/http://www.sungazette.com/page/content.detail/id/505623/Two-indicted-for-2005-killing-at-Allenwood-prison-complex.html|archive-date=March 3, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Pennsylvania Inmate Sentenced To Life In Prison For Violent Murder Of Fellow Inmate|url=https://www.justice.gov/usao/pam/news/2013/Williams_05_15_2013.htm|publisher=US Department of Justice|access-date=12 October 2013|date=May 15, 2013}}</ref> As of March 2022, Williams is currently incarcerated at [[United States Penitentiary, Victorville|USP Victorville]] and Cooya is at [[ADX Florence]].

=== 2020 attack ===
On December 7, 2020, two correctional officers were injured after one was stabbed in the neck and eye by [[Abdulrahman El Bahnasawy|Abdulrahman el Bahnasawy]] (75868-054), a Canadian convicted of terrorism-related offenses in 2016. Both officers were taken via ambulance to [[Geisinger Medical Center]] in [[Danville, Pennsylvania|Danville]] and survived, with one losing an eye.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-01-14|title=Injured Allenwood prison guard to observe a belated Christmas with his family|url=https://www.pennlive.com/news/2020/12/injured-allenwood-prison-guard-to-observe-a-belated-christmas-with-his-family.html|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Farenish|first=Melissa|title=Corrections officer at Allenwood federal prison in critical condition after inmate stabbed him in eye|url=https://www.northcentralpa.com/news/crime/corrections-officer-at-allenwood-federal-prison-in-critical-condition-after-inmate-stabbed-him-in-eye/article_4cd6aeec-395c-11eb-9f12-8f6d2ac82a42.html|access-date=2020-12-10|website=NorthcentralPA.com|date=8 December 2020 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Inmate accused of attacking prison staff in Union County|url=https://www.wnep.com/article/news/local/union-county/prison-inmate-accused-of-attacking-guards-in-union-county/523-bbebcf32-1e46-494c-b2f6-8a214527a0df|access-date=2020-12-10|website=wnep.com|date=8 December 2020 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=It's 'like an attack on all us,' union official says about stabbing of veteran prison guard, HS coach|date=11 December 2020 |url=https://www.pennlive.com/news/2020/12/its-like-an-attack-on-all-us-union-official-says-about-stabbing-of-veteran-prison-guard-hs-coach.html}}</ref> In April 2021, El Bahnasawy was transferred to [[ADX Florence]].
